Application map: every button and every piece of content, and how it is tied to the backend

For each element of the Field-to-Test Loop: what it is, why it exists, when it appears, and an arrow chain that follows it from your click through the browser code, the server address, the Python functions and the database to what the screen shows. Written for a manager who has never seen the application.

571 elements on 12 screens, 125 code excerpts. Built 27 Oct 2026 15:16 by docs/build_ui_map.py from docs/ui_map_src/; every file name and line number below was checked against the current source when this page was built. For the background (what the numbers mean, the learning rules, the lab) read OPERATOR_AND_BACKEND_GUIDE.html.

Start the application and follow along

cd 13_production_app
python3 run_app.py                     # then open http://127.0.0.1:8077 in a browser
python3 run_app.py --standin           # the same, without any AI model calls (deterministic answers)

The server prints one line per request it answers (for example "POST /api/runs/…/act HTTP/1.1" 200). Keep that terminal visible while you click: every arrow chain below ends in exactly such a line.

How the screens are tied to the backend

Every button follows the same nine boxes. The browser function in box 2 is named in each entry below with its file and line; the server function in box 4, the service in 5 and the engine function in 6 likewise. Nothing on the screen changes the database directly: every change goes through one server address and, in the knowledge base, through one function, KGDB.apply_event, which writes the event first and then updates the tables computed from it.

How to read an entry. The left column says what the element is, why it exists and when it appears. The right column is the arrow chain, top to bottom, each step coloured by where it happens:
You · what the person doesBrowser · JavaScript in app/static/jsRequest · what the browser sends to the serverServer address · Flask route in app/api/*.pyService · app/services.py, stage2_service.py, jobs.py, stage1_runner.py, report.pyEngine · the analyser (stage1/pcie_isolate) or the reproduction engine (stage2)Database · db/knowledge.sqlite or db/app.sqlite: events and tablesFiles · files written or read on diskScreen · what you see afterwards
Under each entry, "The code behind it" opens the real source of the functions named in the chain.

Your two questions, answered first

"These many decision tiles: how did they come, why did they come?"

The server decides which decisions to offer for each defect, in available() in stage2/admin_actions.py: ten are always offered (skip, defer, needs more evidence, record a lesson, add a cause, add a procedure, generate test cases, try nearby variations, restart the search, dispute the finding); fourteen more when the lookup found candidates to judge (accept, reject, rank, merge, link, split, delete, undo …); two more (approve, retire) when the defect was seen before. The list travels with the lookup to the screen, where renderView() in review.js sorts it into six groups (Judge, Order or compare, Tidy the knowledge base, Add what you know, Run more in the lab, Put it aside) and tags each tile with what it needs. Each tile exists because the project statement asks that every kind of admin feedback (correct, wrong, partly right, ranking, new knowledge, clean-up) changes what the system shows next time, without training any model. Full chain: "Why exactly these 26 decision tiles appear"; each tile has its own entry, for example Accept.

"The long list of earlier decisions: where does it come from?"

It is read from the event log of the knowledge base: every decision on this error type (from any run), newest first, with the lab result that followed it (Stage2Service.feedback_history, address GET /api/db/feedback/<error type>). On this laptop almost all rows were written by the automated tests (tests/exercise_loop.py and tests/ui_smoke.py), which press the same buttons every few minutes as "admin", with notes such as "exercise: bench silent". A production installation starts with an empty knowledge base and shows only real decisions. Full chain: "Where the Earlier decisions rows come from".

Sidebar

1

Field-to-Test Loop · PCIe trace → defects found → reproduced → tested

display

What it is: The name of the application and, under it, the whole loop in four words: a PCIe (PCI Express, the bus between the computer and the drive) trace goes in, defects are found, each defect is reproduced in the lab, and it ends as a test.

Why it exists: The project statement asks for one closed loop from field failure to long-term validation; the line tells a newcomer the order of the work before any button is pressed.

How it works, step by step
  1. Files
    app/static/index.html: the text is written in the page file itself (the sidebar head); nothing is computed.
    app/static/index.html:12 · browser code
  2. ↓
  3. Server address
    The Flask route for / sends the page file unchanged.
    app/server.py:32 · create_app
  4. ↓
  5. Request
    GET /
  6. ↓
  7. Screen
    The text is shown as written, the same for every run.

complete · 14.7 s

display

What it is: The line under step 2. While stage 1 runs: the current step in short words and the percentage, with a thin bar (for example "reading packets · 42%"). Afterwards "complete · <seconds> s", or "failed". Without a run: "locked · complete step 1 first".

Why it exists: Stage 1 of a large trace takes minutes (the 4 GB trace in this installation took 1,326.6 s); the line keeps the progress visible while you look at other pages.

When: Updated whenever the run list is re-read (every 1.5 seconds while step 2 watches a running analysis).

4 Reproduce and decide (stage 2)

button

What it is: Opens step 4 (stage 2): first the "Start stage 2" gate, after that the queue of defects to review. Described in detail in the step-4 parts of this map.

0 of 5 steps completed · 5 remaining

display

What it is: The step counter under the five steps. Step 1 counts as soon as a run is selected; steps 2 and 3 when its stage 1 has finished; steps 4 and 5 when every defect with a catalogue match has a decision (phase "stage 2 complete"). " · stage 1 failed" is added after a failure.

Why it exists: One number tells a manager how far the selected run is through the loop.

When: Recomputed whenever the run list is re-read.

Sidebar foot

16

AI reviewer Anthropic claude-haiku-5-5

display

What it is: Which AI (artificial intelligence) model answers as "AI reviewer": "Anthropic <model>", "Ollama <model>", "OpenAI-compatible <model>" or "stand-in (no model)" when no model can be reached.

Why it exists: Every second opinion and every stage-2 proposal depends on this model; the operator must see which one is in use before trusting an answer.

When: Set once when the application loads. After Save on the Settings page the raw name (for example anthropic:claude-haiku-5-5:low) is written here until the page is reloaded. The name is the stage-2 reviewer; stage 1 reaches a model only with the cli, sdk or auto backend (openai-compat runs its review without one).

Example from this installation: llm_active "anthropic:claude-haiku-5-5:low" is shown as "Anthropic claude-haiku-5-5" in this installation (backend "cli").
How it works, step by step
  1. Files
    config/app_config.json section llm: backend, model, effort.
  2. ↓
  3. Service
    make_llm() builds the AI reviewer object for stage 2 from that section; its name is for example anthropic:<model>:<effort>, or stand-in when the backend is not reachable.
    app/stage2_service.py:32 · make_llm
  4. ↓
  5. Server address
    llm_active = the name of that object.
    app/api/config_api.py:17 · get_config

  8. ↓

lab device simulated device

display

What it is: Where stage 2 runs its lab runs: "simulated device" (the built-in simulated drive) or "real device" (a real drive connected through app/bench_hook.py).

Why it exists: A reproduction on a simulated drive is not the same proof as one on the real drive; the operator must know which one produced a result.

When: Set once when the application loads; a change in Settings takes effect after a restart.

Example from this installation: stage2.bench is "synthetic" in this installation, shown as "simulated device".

Choose the trace

Why it exists: Confirms where you are, in the same words as the sidebar.

When: Changes with every page switch.

How it works, step by step

Analyzer CSV path required

field

What it is: The full path, on the server's disk, of the 113-column export from the LeCroy or VIAVI analyzer, for example /home/you/captures/trace.csv. The grey line under it says the path must lie under one of the folders the administrator allowed (config/app_config.json).

Why it exists: The packets are the evidence for every rule, defect and proof. Only the path is sent because captures are too big to upload (this installation holds a 4 GB one); the folder check stops the screen from being used to read arbitrary files of the server.

When: Required: the browser refuses to start without it ("the CSV path is required").

Example from this installation: Allowed folders in this installation: "~", "/tmp", "/mnt", "/media" plus the application folder. Example path: /home/raghavendra/Desktop/Project_Implmentation/13_production_app/samples/sample_T-42_L-21_C-16_seed11.csv (23.1 MB, about 47,413 rows).

4

Payload sidecar (the bytes inside the packets; only for size-only exports)

field

What it is: Optional path of a separate file that holds the bytes inside the packets, for analyzer exports whose DATA column shows only sizes such as "256 B".

Why it exists: The NVMe (NVM Express, the drive's command protocol) rules read commands, completions, PRP lists (the memory page lists of a command) and registers from those bytes; without them those rules cannot run and step 2 warns that the trace was analysed with limited inputs.

When: Leave empty when the export already carries the bytes ("inline hex").

Example from this installation: Not needed for the sample traces of this installation: their run.json says payload "inline hex".

Linux kernel log (dmesg -x)

field

What it is: Optional path of the host computer's kernel log, saved with dmesg -x (each line with its level and time). It sits under the sub-heading "Host evidence, for defects that leave no trace in the packets (optional, recommended)".

Why it exists: Some failures are visible only on the host (driver timeouts, garbage configuration reads, management actions); the kernel log lets stage 1 prove them instead of reporting them as "Needs evidence".

When: Optional. When given (or host_events.jsonl), the step "Line up the host evidence with the packets" runs. A log without any "resetting controller" line, or a trace without a controller reset, cannot be aligned: the step stops and stage 1 fails.

Example from this installation: The runs of this installation were made without host evidence (step 2 shows "no host evidence given").

Host tool records (host_events.jsonl)

field

What it is: Optional path of a file with one JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) record per line from host tools: {"time", "source" (nvme-log, smart-log, fio-verify, blktrace, lspci, bmc, ...), "level", "text"}.

Namespace size (nsze, from Identify Namespace)

field

What it is: Optional size of the drive's namespace in logical blocks (nsze, as reported by Identify Namespace), for example 0x3A386030.

Why it exists: Lets the address-range rules tell an out-of-range read or write (a logical block address beyond the end of the namespace) from a valid one.

When: Optional. Pre-filled from config stage1.nsze when set; the analyser also takes the value from an Identify Namespace answer found in the trace.

Example from this installation: Run run-20261026-145008-0220 was started with nsze "0x3A386030".

Delete

What it is: Deletes the run after a confirmation ("Delete run <id> (<file>)? This removes its stage 1 results, stage 2 state and logs. The knowledge base (your decisions, procedures, tests) is kept. This cannot be undone.").

Why it exists: Run folders grow (the 4 GB trace's run is large); deleting must never touch the knowledge base, which is learned state shared by all runs, not run data.

When: Disabled while the run is queued or running. The server also refuses while a stage-2 job of the run is still working ("a stage-2 job of this run is still in progress - wait for it to finish").

Stop the analysis

button

What it is: Asks to stop the running analysis, after the confirmation "Stop the analysis of this trace? It stops after the step that is running now; the run is then marked failed. Its partial files stay in the run folder (Delete in Earlier runs removes them). You can analyse the file again later." The message "stop requested" appears.

When: The button is always shown, also on a finished run, where the request changes nothing. A running analysis stops only when its current step ends (the analyser's long reading step is not interrupted).

Progress

4

100%

display

What it is: The progress ring with the percentage in the middle. Each step owns a share: reading packets 2-60 % (moving with the rows read), host evidence 60-64 %, grouping 64-72 %, reusing verdicts 73 %, AI reviewer 74-94 %, report 95-97 %, capture check 97-99 %. It shows 100 % only when the job is done (at most 99 % before).

Why it exists: An honest progress view: the operator can tell a long, healthy analysis from a stuck one.

When: Shown while a run is selected on step 2; green when done, red when failed.

9

Read the capture and check every packet

row

What it is: The first and longest step: one pass over the CSV, row by row. Each row goes to the checks for its kind (transaction packets, acknowledgements, ordered sets, link events, markers); whenever the state the specification defines goes wrong, a rule fires. The count on the right: "<rows read> of about <rows> packets read · <n> rules fired".

Why it exists: This is where the evidence comes from; the live count shows the analyser is moving through a large file. The total is estimated from the file size because counting the lines of a 4 GB file would take as long as reading it.

When: The count is updated every 2,000,000 rows and at the end of the step; the number of rules fired is replaced at the grouping step by the final count (host and whole-trace findings included).

Example from this installation: "42,906 of about 47,413 packets read · 30 rules fired" for run run-20261026-145008-0220.

12

Reuse AI reviewer verdicts from earlier runs (no model call)

row

What it is: For each defect a key is built from error type, first rule, error family, layer, the set of rules, the sequence of packet kinds in its rows, the model and the prompt version; a verdict stored under that key earlier is reused. The count: "<n> verdicts reused".

Why it exists: The same pattern confirmed once does not need to be paid for again; a model or prompt change changes the key, so an old verdict is never reused for a new model.

13

Ask the AI reviewer for a second opinion on each defect

row

What it is: The defects not answered by the cache are sent, with their packet rows and rule texts, to the AI reviewer, which answers whether the rows show the defect, which rules it agrees with, which packets it cites and who caused it. The count: "<n> of <m> reviewed".

Why it exists: Rules can fire for the wrong reason; a second opinion that must cite packets catches that, without ever overruling the rules.

When: Skipped (–) when the backend runs without a model (stand-in, openai-compat) or when every defect already got a cached verdict; the right column then says "no AI reviewer configured" or, when every verdict came from the cache, "not needed: every verdict was reused from the cache". The live count arrives every 25 defects (command-line backend) or 50 (programming-interface backend).

Example from this installation: Run run-20261026-145008-0220 shows "not needed: every verdict was reused from the cache": the backend "cli" is configured, and all three verdicts came from the cache.

The defect page

Where: http://127.0.0.1:8077/defect?run=<run>&inc=<defect> · 58 elements on this screen, numbered in the picture and below.

Header

1

Full record of one defect

display

What it is: A read-only page with everything about one defect, in the order a newcomer reads it: a header card, then eight sections (what it means, where, why flagged, evidence packets, what usually fixes it, related error types, stage 2, earlier decisions). It is opened from "Open the full record ↗" in step 2 and loads everything with one request.

Why it exists: Step 2 shows only a summary; a person who must decide or explain a defect needs every rule, packet and earlier decision in one place, shareable as one address.

When: Opened in a new tab; the address names the run and the defect.

Example from this installation: http://127.0.0.1:8077/defect?run=run-20261026-145008-0220&inc=INC-0001

Proof checks: ✓ capture context given · ✓ knock-on effects separated by the analyser · …

display

What it is: Eight yes/no checks of the conclusion, each ✓ or ✗: capture context given, every claim cites a packet that was shown, knock-on effects separated by the analyser, first abnormal packet identified, other explanations labelled as such, reproduced by the analyser on the full file, root cause and knock-on effects cited from shown packets, a rule is named.

Why it exists: An AI-assisted conclusion is accepted only if these checks pass (the acceptance test for an AI conclusion); they are evaluated mechanically, not by the model.

When: Only when the record carries the checks.

6 · Related error types

45

Error types the analyser scored

display

What it is: The three best catalogue matches, one per line: short error type, "match <score>" and the first 60 characters of the title. The score is the similarity of the defect's rule pattern to the card's learned signature, weighted by the error-family vote.

The code behind it (2 excerpts)

What you see

7

preparing: Defect 2 (2 of 3) · 4.5 s

display

What it is: The live line under the button while the preparation runs: which defect is being prepared and the seconds since the job started.

Why it exists: The AI reviewer call takes seconds per defect; the line shows that work is going on. Behind it, every defect is looked up and stored so that it opens at once later.

Example from this installation: live: the three lookups took 27.6 s, 23.9 s and 33.7 s (view timings present_s), almost all of it the AI reviewer.
How it works, step by step
  1. Service
    For each defect the job opens a timing span "stage2.present.<defect>" (its start writes "running") and, inside it, writes the progress text "INC-000N (n of m)" and the percentage, so that text stays visible during the whole lookup.
    app/api/stage2_api.py:180 · _prepare
  2. ↓
  3. Service
    Stage2Service.present: sets the event metadata, runs the engine under the lock, commits, builds the view (saved procedure, AI proposal, seen-before label, offered actions, timings) and stores view and context in the defect's state file.
    app/stage2_service.py:165 · Stage2Service.present
  4. ↓
  5. Engine
    Stage2V3.present: event incident_seen; a query from the defect (error type, family, first rule, layer, origin, verdict, device-and-firmware fingerprint, tokens, packet kinds); HybridIndex.query returns the 5 best records; seen_before; event impression (which records were shown at which position); the evidence text (25 rows).
    stage2/stage2_v3.py:99 · Stage2V3.present

Seen before on this firmware - the saved procedure applies

display

What it is: Green pill "seen before" = match: the same defect is already in the knowledge base for this device and firmware, so the saved procedure should apply as it is.

Why it exists: The main saving of the knowledge base: a defect seen before is reproduced by re-running its saved procedure (seconds, no search, no model call) instead of a new search.

When: When the best procedure among the 5 shown records has the same error type AND the same device-and-firmware fingerprint AND a lookup match of at least 0.70 AND the structured match is at least 1.375 (the error type plus at least 2 of the 4 fields first rule, layer, who caused it, verdict agree). Lookups stored before 27 October 2026 show the older wording "YES - same defect seen before in this context; stored procedure applies" until the lookup is redone.

15

Seen before on another firmware - start from the saved procedure (and the other "related" sentences)

display

What it is: Yellow pill "related" = ambiguous: something close is saved, but not the same defect in the same context. Sentences: "Seen before on this firmware, but a different rule fired first - start from the saved procedure", "Seen before on another firmware - start from the saved procedure", "Not seen before, but error type X fails the same way and has a procedure", "Not seen before, but a capture with the same packet pattern (X) has a procedure".

Why it exists: A related procedure is a good starting point but must be checked: Correct on it re-runs it first (same error type) or uses it to seed the search (other error type).

When: When the best procedure is not a match but has the same error type, or the same failure family, or a strongly similar packet sequence (sequence score at least 0.5, structured match at least 0.4 and lookup match at least 0.35).

The code behind it (1 excerpt)
19

Look up again

button

What it is: Repeats the lookup of this defect: the knowledge base is searched again and the AI reviewer is asked again for its proposal (one model call), even when nothing was decided since.

Why it exists: Other admins may have decided on the same error type, or new procedures were filed, since the lookup; the cards should reflect the current knowledge base. A lookup is otherwise served from disk to save model calls, so repeating it is a deliberate click.

When: Always enabled except while a request runs. Each click costs one AI reviewer call (the model answer may come from the prompt cache db/llm_cache.jsonl when the prompt is identical).

How it works, step by step
  1. You
    You click Look up again.
  2. ↓
  3. Browser
    The click handler calls present(true): the button is disabled and the line says "looking up the knowledge base and asking the AI reviewer…".
    app/static/js/review.js:77 · browser code
  4. ↓
  5. Request
    POST /api/runs/<run>/incidents/<defect>/present?force=1 (no body)
  6. ↓

When: For rows whose "Link Dir" field is Downstream or Upstream.

— 50 ms gap, no traffic —

display

What it is: A yellow band between two rows that are 1 ms or more apart.

Why it exists: Long pauses are often the trigger (a recovery time not respected, an idle period entering a low-power state); the band makes them impossible to miss.

When: When the time difference between two drawn rows is at least 1000 µs. In the short view left-out acknowledgements may lie inside the band, so "no traffic" means no drawn packet.

Drag to rank, best first. Judge each one: Correct runs it in the lab and writes the regression test · Needs changes opens it for editing · Not correct removes it (undo any time). A procedure validated in the lab stays "awaiting approval by a second admin" until a second admin approves it (two-person rule).

What it is: The instruction above the cards.

Why it exists: The three verdicts are the whole decision for most defects; the two-person rule (four-eyes principle) protects the knowledge base from one person's mistake.

When: Adds "(the order is recorded once two or more saved procedures exist)" when fewer than two saved procedures are listed. Note: "undo any time" holds until Save decisions; after saving, the message offers no Undo.

The code behind it (1 excerpt)

Card buttons

49

① Correct

button

What it is: You confirm that this procedure reproduces the defect: it is credited, run in the lab (a saved one is re-run first), checked on known-bad and fixed firmware and filed as a regression test.

Why it exists: The admin's acceptance is the positive feedback of the loop and the start of the closed-loop test: the statement's "admin decides, the system reproduces and converts it into a test".

When: On every card that is not removed. Key 1 on a focused card does the same. Unsaved removals and a new ranking are saved first.

Example from this installation: live, Defect 1, first decision: accept -> mode reuse, status reused_validated, test filed; Defect 3: accept -> mode adapt, 18 trials, reproduced 8 of 8, test filed.
How it works, step by step
  1. You
    You click ① Correct (or press 1).
  2. ↓
  3. Browser
    verdict(…, "correct") disables the card's buttons, counts it in "Your decision", saves pending removals / ranking (commitPending), then review.js act("accept"): busy line "accepted: running it in the lab, …"; target = the card id for a saved procedure, else the cause of the lookup; with no cause it becomes add_cause with the AI headline as text.
    app/static/js/review.js:198 · browser code
  4. ↓
  5. Request
    POST /api/runs/<run>/incidents/<defect>/act {"action":"accept","requester":"<your name>","approver":"","targets":["sol::<procedure hash>"],"note":""} (accept never carries a second-admin name) (AI proposal: "targets":["cause::T-42::c0"]; no cause: {"action":"add_cause","targets":[],"content":{"text":"<AI headline>"}})
  6. ↓
  7. Server address
    Refuses with code 409 unless stage 1 has finished and stage 2 was started for this run (the order check _gate), then passes the decision, the run's firmware label and the run's metadata (who started it, trace, device) to the stage-2 service. The answer is {"result": …, "job": …}; code 400 only when the result itself is an error.
    app/api/stage2_api.py:290 · act
  8. ↓
  9. Service
    This is one of the seven lab actions (SEARCH_ACTIONS: accept, accept_with_note, add_cause, add_procedure, compose_tests, sweep, restart_failed), so it does not run while you wait: the service stamps the same metadata, counts the earlier failed attempts of this defect (the attempt number picks another random stream) and starts a background job of kind "stage2" in db/app.sqlite table job; the answer is only the job number.
    app/stage2_service.py:202 · Stage2Service.act
  10. ↓
  11. Engine
    Stage2V3.execute -> admin_actions.apply "accept": event admin_action (decision, targets, the shown list, run, defect); for a procedure: proc_credit r = 1 on its procedure edge and node and verdict "correct" on its cause (lab_result true); for a cause: verdict "correct". add_cause: node_create c<N> + verdict.
    stage2/admin_actions.py:136 · apply
  12. ↓
  13. Database
    db/knowledge.sqlite: edge error type -> cause: all causes fade 2 %, then a + 1, n + 1, ta + 1 (lab count); case_memory row; pedge REPRODUCED_BY and pnode of the procedure a + 1, n + 1; CAUSED_BY mirrors the edge.
    stage2/kgdb.py:213 · KGDB._project
  14. ↓
  15. Engine
    Way: reuse (saved procedure of THIS error type: 6 runs, ≥ 3 reproduce -> no search) · adapt (another error type's procedure, or the saved one regressed: lesson, then search) · generate (AI proposal / cause: search). Then Optimizer.search, minimize, stress_ascent and _finish: verify_closed_loop, test_manifest + emit_closed_loop_test, events solution_propose / solution_validate / script_gate (see the busy line entry).
    stage2/stage2_v3.py:159 · Stage2V3.execute
  16. ↓
  17. Files
    runs/<run>/stage2/<defect>.json: the result is appended to "results" and becomes "last" (the queue then counts the defect as decided). suite/T-<error type>-<device>-<procedure>/manifest.json, test_*.py, conftest.py (and a second folder for the most stressful version).
  18. ↓
  19. Screen
    Every 2 seconds the page asks GET /api/jobs/<job> (poll in api.js) and updates the busy line "working… N s — …"; when the job is done the message "stage 2 finished: <outcome>" appears with an Undo button for 8 seconds, the sidebar and the queue are refreshed, the defect is opened again and the Result section is drawn from the new "last" result.
    app/static/js/review.js:299 · browser code

When: Refused with a message when no command is left ("add at least one command") or nothing changed ("nothing changed — use Correct if it is right as saved").

Example from this installation: test copy: flush, write, 300 µs, idle 600 ms -> mode admin_procedure, 6 of 6, bound 0.61, test filed, most stressful version filed too.
How it works, step by step
  1. You
    You click Save corrected version.
  2. ↓
  3. Browser
    Checks commands and changes, disables the card's buttons, counts it as corrected, saves pending removals / ranking, then act("procedure"): busy line "validating your version: …"; doAction("add_procedure") with your version; the target is the lookup's cause only for the AI proposal.
    app/static/js/decision.js:348 · browser code
  4. ↓
  5. Request
    POST /api/runs/<run>/incidents/<defect>/act {"action":"add_procedure","requester":"<your name>","approver":"","targets":[],"note":"","content":{"commands":[{"op":"flush"},{"op":"write"}],"timing":{"qd":8,"inter_cmd_us":300,"bs_kb":4,"burst_len":16,"idle_gap_ms":600},"power_state":"none"}}
  6. ↓
  7. Server address
    Refuses with code 409 unless stage 1 has finished and stage 2 was started for this run (the order check _gate), then passes the decision, the run's firmware label and the run's metadata (who started it, trace, device) to the stage-2 service. The answer is {"result": …, "job": …}; code 400 only when the result itself is an error.
    app/api/stage2_api.py:290 · act
  8. ↓
  9. Service
    This is one of the seven lab actions (SEARCH_ACTIONS: accept, accept_with_note, add_cause, add_procedure, compose_tests, sweep, restart_failed), so it does not run while you wait: the service stamps the same metadata, counts the earlier failed attempts of this defect (the attempt number picks another random stream) and starts a background job of kind "stage2" in db/app.sqlite table job; the answer is only the job number.
    app/stage2_service.py:202 · Stage2Service.act
  10. ↓
  11. Engine
    apply "add_procedure": clean_scenario refuses unknown commands ("procedure rejected: …"), clamps timing to the lab ranges, replaces an unknown power state by none; procedure id = first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 hash of the cleaned procedure; events admin_action and solution_propose (producer "admin:<your name>", status proposed).
    stage2/admin_actions.py:274 · apply
  12. ↓
  13. Engine
    execute: your version is run 6 times on the device model. ≥ 3 reproduce -> mode admin_procedure, status confirmed, most stressful conditions (stress_ascent), _finish validates it under its own hash (solution_validate with the Wilson lower bound of k of 6); the lab check and the test files follow only when that bound is ≥ 0.5, i.e. 6 of 6. < 3 -> solution_validate 0 (failed-validation), lesson "your procedure showed the error in k of 6 runs - not enough; the search starts from it", then the search from your version (mode adapt).
    stage2/stage2_v3.py:159 · Stage2V3.execute
  14. ↓
  15. Database
    db/knowledge.sqlite: solution row (proposed -> validated-by-execution or failed-validation), pnode scenario + pedge REPRODUCED_BY, lesson row on failure, artifact rows for script_gate; no credit to the old procedure.
    stage2/kgdb.py:274 · KGDB._project
  16. ↓
  17. Files
    runs/<run>/stage2/<defect>.json: the result is appended to "results" and becomes "last" (the queue then counts the defect as decided). suite/T-…/ when the lab check ran.
  18. ↓
  19. Screen
    After the job: the Result section with "Your version reproduced the defect in k of 6 lab runs and was saved under your name." (with 3-5 of 6 the headline says it was too few for the lab check; Correct on it confirms it with more runs) or "Your version did not reproduce the defect reliably (k of 6 lab runs); … The lab searched from it and found the version below."

also retire it from the knowledge base (needs a second admin)

checkbox

What it is: When ticked, Save decisions also retires (deprecates) the approved procedure after recording the rejection, so it is no longer offered. Because retiring needs two people, the page asks for the second admin's name at that moment.

Why it exists: A wrong approved procedure should stop being recommended; retiring needs two people because it removes approved knowledge.

  3. Browser

What it is: Sends every pending removal (with its reason, and retire if ticked) and, if you reordered at least two saved procedures, your ranking.

Why it exists: Negative feedback and orderings are what keep the knowledge base honest: only the rejected item loses credit, and an order is a rating, never a success.

When: Disabled when nothing is pending. Also triggered automatically before Correct and Save corrected version.

Example from this installation: test copy: reject with note "Wrong timing" -> effects ["marked not correct (-1)"], events 14 and 15.
How it works, step by step
  1. You
    You click Save decisions.
  2. ↓
  3. Browser
    commitPending: one act("reject") per removed card, then act("rerank") with the new order; then the message "decisions saved" and the defect is reloaded. review.js act: a saved procedure -> doAction("reject"); the AI proposal (not stored) -> doAction("lesson", "NOT CORRECT: the AI reviewer's new proposal (<title>) — <reason>"); retire -> deprecate; rerank -> the saved procedures in your order.
    app/static/js/decision.js:244 · browser code

    POST /api/runs/<run>/incidents/<defect>/act {"action":"reject","requester":"<your name>","approver":"","targets":["sol::<hash>"],"note":"Wrong timing"} · {"action":"lesson",…,"targets":["cause::T-42::c0"],"note":"NOT CORRECT: the AI reviewer's new proposal (…) — Wrong timing"} · {"action":"rerank",…,"targets":["sol::a","sol::b"],"ranking":["sol::a","sol::b"],"note":""}

    Refuses with code 409 unless stage 1 has finished and stage 2 was started for this run (the order check _gate), then passes the decision, the run's firmware label and the run's metadata (who started it, trace, device) to the stage-2 service. The answer is {"result": …, "job": …}; code 400 only when the result itself is an error.

    Rejects an unknown action name, loads the defect's saved lookup (from memory or from its state file), fills in the error type and the requester (your name; if empty the run's operator, else "admin"), stamps every event it writes with run, trace, defect, device, serial number, firmware and person, applies the decision under the stage-2 lock, commits it to disk at once and appends the result to the defect's state file.
    app/stage2_service.py:202 · Stage2Service.act

    apply: reject -> admin_action + proc_credit r = 0 on that procedure's edge only (nothing else is punished); lesson -> admin_action + lesson "ADMIN NOTE: NOT CORRECT: …" (the next AI prompt reads the lessons); rerank -> admin_action + proc_rank with the procedure order.

Generate test cases from the knowledge base

93

The database holds 5 correct / optimised sequences (saved procedures) for this error type. The AI reviewer composes up to three test variants from them …

display

What it is: How many saved procedures of this error type exist (and of the same family), and what composing will do: up to three variants - a robust recreation, the same trigger at its timing boundary, a different path to the same state - each run in the lab and filed only if the analyser finds this defect. Without a saved procedure: "No saved sequence for this error type yet. Judge one Correct first …". For a workload record (ADK / PCMark tool output): it says that only the hardware bench can run it.

Why it exists: One reproduction gives one test; a fix that only covers that exact path would still pass. Composition turns earned knowledge into a small family of tests at no search cost.

When: Shown once the cards are loaded.

Example from this installation: live, Defect 1: "The database holds 5 correct / optimised sequences (saved procedures) for this error type."

101

✓ Reproduced and checked — regression test written / ! Reproduced in k of n lab runs, too few for the lab check (…), so no check ran and no test was filed — press Correct on it to confirm it with more runs / ! Reproduced, but the lab check on known-bad and fixed firmware did not pass it, so no test was filed / ✕ Not reproduced within the limits

display

What it is: The verdict of the reproduction in one line: green = the lab check passed and the test is filed; yellow = reproduced but too rarely for the lab check, or reproduced but the check did not pass; red = not reproduced.

Why it exists: The single most important answer for a manager.

When: Green when admitted. Yellow "too few for the lab check" when the status is confirmed or reused_validated and no lab check ran - in practice your corrected version with 3-5 of 6 reproductions, whose safe lower estimate stays below 50 % ("Reproduced in 4 of 6 lab runs, too few for the lab check (it needs a safe estimate of at least 50 %: 6 of 6 with six runs), so no check ran and no test was filed — press Correct on it to confirm it with more runs"). Yellow "did not pass" when the check ran and failed (its test files are then listed as written for inspection only). Red otherwise.

110

Record the failed attempt (−1) and restart the search

button

What it is: Records the failed attempt as negative feedback, writes a lesson, and starts the search again on a different random stream.

Why it exists: The diagram's "Negative Ack (−1)": a search that failed within the limits is counted against what was tried, and the next attempt explores differently instead of repeating the same path.

When: Only when the last status is not reproduced, trial budget used up, triage limit exceeded, or your version did not reproduce. Note: the target is the cause found by the lookup, so the −1 lands on the cause (and its lab count), not on a procedure; with no cause only the lesson is written.

Example from this installation: live, Defect 2: last status budget_exhausted after 301 trials, so the button is shown.
How it works, step by step
  1. You
    You click the button.
  2. ↓
  3. Browser
    The button is disabled; act("restart") shows "failed attempt recorded (−1); the search restarts with a different random seed…" and sends restart_failed with the note "no reproduction within the limits (<outcome>)".
    app/static/js/review.js:193 · browser code
  4. ↓
  5. Request
    POST /api/runs/<run>/incidents/<defect>/act {"action":"restart_failed","requester":"<your name>","approver":"","targets":["cause::M-020::c0"],"note":"no reproduction within the limits (not reproduced (trial budget used up))"}
  6. ↓
  7. Server address
    Refuses with code 409 unless stage 1 has finished and stage 2 was started for this run (the order check _gate), then passes the decision, the run's firmware label and the run's metadata (who started it, trace, device) to the stage-2 service. The answer is {"result": …, "job": …}; code 400 only when the result itself is an error.
    app/api/stage2_api.py:290 · act
  8. ↓
  9. Service
    This is one of the seven lab actions (SEARCH_ACTIONS: accept, accept_with_note, add_cause, add_procedure, compose_tests, sweep, restart_failed), so it does not run while you wait: the service stamps the same metadata, counts the earlier failed attempts of this defect (the attempt number picks another random stream) and starts a background job of kind "stage2" in db/app.sqlite table job; the answer is only the job number.
    app/stage2_service.py:202 · Stage2Service.act
  10. ↓
  11. Engine
    apply "restart_failed": for a cause verdict "not" (b + 1) and verdict "lab" (tb + 1); for a procedure proc_credit r = 0; always a lesson "FAILED TRIAL recorded by …; the search starts again: …".
    stage2/admin_actions.py:245 · apply
  12. ↓
  13. Engine
    execute: attempt n -> the search's random seed is shifted by 10 × n; mode generate from the cause; then the same search, shortening, lab check and test files as Correct.
    stage2/stage2_v3.py:159 · Stage2V3.execute
  14. ↓

    db/knowledge.sqlite: edge error type -> cause b + 1 and tb + 1 (after the 2 % fading), lesson row; new solution / script_gate events if the new search finds something.
  16. ↓

    Every 2 seconds the page asks GET /api/jobs/<job> (poll in api.js) and updates the busy line "working… N s — …"; when the job is done the message "stage 2 finished: <outcome>" appears with an Undo button for 8 seconds, the sidebar and the queue are refreshed, the defect is opened again and the Result section is drawn from the new "last" result.
    app/static/js/review.js:299 · browser code

The code behind it (1 excerpt)

Step 4 · All details: candidates, the 26 decisions, editor, history

Where: the "All details" box at the bottom of step 4 · 119 elements on this screen, numbered in the picture and below.

Why these things are here

1

Why exactly these 26 decision tiles appear

display

What it is: Step 2 of the form ("What do you want to do?") shows one tile per decision the knowledge base understands, sorted into six groups. The list of decisions is not written in the page: the server decides which decisions make sense for this defect when it looks the defect up, and the page only draws them. The full vocabulary is the 26 names in ALL in stage2/admin_actions.py (7 verdicts on a record, 3 orderings, 10 life-cycle decisions, 6 structure decisions). available(seen_before, has_candidates) picks from it: 10 are always offered (Skip, Defer, Needs more evidence, Record a lesson, Add a cause, Add a procedure, Generate test cases, Try nearby variations, Restart the search after a failed attempt, Dispute the stage-1 finding); 14 more when the lookup found at least one record (Accept, Accept with a note, Revise the text, Reject, Could not be reproduced, Record my ranking, Prefer this one, Tie, Mark as a duplicate, Link to another, Split, Request deletion, Approve the deletion, Undo a decision); 2 more (Approve as second admin, Retire the procedure) only when the lookup says the defect was seen before ("match" or "ambiguous"), because only then is there a saved procedure to approve or retire. 10 + 14 + 2 = 26. The page groups them with GROUPS in review.js: (1) "Judge the ticked procedure" - Accept, Accept with a note, Revise the text, Reject, Could not be reproduced: a verdict on one record; (2) "Order or compare procedures" - Record my ranking, Prefer this one, Tie: relative judgements; (3) "Tidy the knowledge base" - Approve as second admin, Retire the procedure, Mark as a duplicate, Link to another, Split, Request deletion, Approve the deletion: the life cycle and structure of stored records; (4) "Add what you know" - Record a lesson, Add a cause, Add a procedure, Needs more evidence, Dispute the stage-1 finding: knowledge the system does not have; (5) "Run more in the lab" - Generate test cases, Try nearby variations, Restart the search after a failed attempt; (6) "Put it aside" - Skip, Defer, Undo a decision. Each tile shows its name (actionWord in decision.js), a one-line meaning (ACTION_HELP in app/api/__init__.py, sent to the page by GET /api/config) and grey tags from NEED and TAGS in review.js saying what it needs ("needs one ticked record", "needs two ticked records", "needs an order (click the candidates)", "asks for a reason", "needs a second admin", "asks which decision", "runs in the lab, takes minutes"). Green tiles (Accept, Accept with a note, Add a cause) give credit, red tiles (Reject, Could not be reproduced, Dispute) take it away, yellow tiles (Approve as second admin, Retire the procedure, Approve the deletion) need two people.

Why it exists: The project asks that the administrator's feedback - positive, negative, partial, re-ordering - teaches the knowledge base without training a model. Every kind of feedback therefore needs its own, precisely defined decision, because each one changes different counters (a correct cause must not be blamed when only the lab bench failed; an order is not a success). The groups exist so a manager can find a decision by intent: judging one record, comparing records, keeping the knowledge base tidy under a two-person rule, adding knowledge, asking for more lab work, or not deciding now (not deciding is deliberately not a signal). Offering only what makes sense (no Approve when nothing was seen before) prevents decisions that could only fail.

When: Shown when All details is open, after the defect was looked up. A group whose decisions are all missing from the offered list is left out.

Example from this installation: On this page (run run-20261026-145008-0220, Defect 1, error type T-42, seen before = match) only 23 tiles in 5 groups are drawn: the view in runs/run-20261026-145008-0220/stage2/INC-0001.json was saved by the lookup of 26 Oct 2026 14:50, and its action list has no compose_tests, sweep or restart_failed, which the current available() always offers (stage2/admin_actions.py was changed on 27 Oct 2026 00:53). "Look up again" would store the current list of 26. Scratch copy: a never-seen error type got 24 tiles (seen before = new, so no Approve / Retire); after one decision the same defect was a match and got all 26.

    stage2/admin_actions.py:49 · available

The code behind it (2 excerpts)
2

Where the 'Earlier decisions on this error type' rows come from and why there are so many

display

What it is: The table at the bottom of the tab lists every decision any admin recorded on this error type (here T-42), from any run and any defect, newest first, at most 50. It is read from the event table of the knowledge base: Stage2Service.feedback_history selects the admin_action events and the script_gate events (the lab check that files a regression test) whose payload names this error type and that were not undone; each decision is paired with the next lab check of the same error type, which becomes its "Lab outcome". Each decision gets a polarity: positive = Accept, Accept with a note, Approve as second admin, Add a procedure, Add a cause; negative = Reject, Could not be reproduced, Dispute the stage-1 finding, Retire the procedure, Request deletion, Approve the deletion, and a lesson whose note starts with "NOT CORRECT" (what "Not correct" on the AI (artificial intelligence) reviewer's proposal writes on the main screen); everything else is neutral. Why so many rows on this laptop: the database was filled mostly by the automated tests. tests/exercise_loop.py drives the running application through captures with T-42 (cards "T-42,L-21,C-16" and "T-42,L-21,M-039") and sends, as requester "admin", accept, compose_tests, sweep, reject (note "exercise: timing is wrong for this firmware"), add_procedure, rerank, not_reproducible (note "exercise: bench silent"), revise, deprecate (then undone), skip, defer and escalate (note "exercise"), plus add_cause when nothing is stored and restart_failed when a defect did not reproduce. tests/ui_smoke.py drives this very screen in a browser (ranking + Save decisions, Not correct on the proposal, Save corrected version, Correct, Generate test cases, Try nearby variations); when "Your name" is empty the server records "admin". Every run of these tests adds the same dozen rows again. A production database starts empty (stage2/kgdb.py: "The database starts EMPTY") and contains only real decisions.

Why it exists: The project requires that every decision is kept with who, when and why, and that the next person sees earlier negative feedback before trusting a saved procedure. Pairing a decision with the lab check that followed shows whether the decision held up in the lab.

When: Loaded each time a defect is shown (after the lookup), for that defect's error type.

Example from this installation: Read-only on 27 Oct 2026: the event table holds 1178 events; 162 are admin_action events for T-42 (11 of them undone - the exercise's deprecate + undo), 160 by "admin" and 2 by "tester one"; their notes are "exercise: timing is wrong for this firmware" (11), "exercise: bench silent" (11), "exercise" (9), three "NOT CORRECT: the LLM's new proposal …" lessons and 128 empty notes. The first is from 26 Oct 2026 13:27, the newest from 27 Oct 2026 12:59 (Try nearby variations by admin). Of the 151 that were not undone the table shows the newest 50.
How it works, step by step

    db/knowledge.sqlite, table event: rows of kind admin_action (written first by every decision) and script_gate (written by the lab check); undone = 0 only; payload LIKE '%"sig": "T-42"%'.

    Stage2Service.feedback_history(sig, limit=50) builds one row per admin_action (event id, time, actor, decision, targets, note, second admin, defect, run, polarity) and attaches the first following script_gate of the same error type as outcome {admitted, known_bad hits/runs, fixed hits/runs}; returns the newest 50.
    app/stage2_service.py:301 · Stage2Service.feedback_history
  4. ↓
  5. Server address
    The route takes the stage-2 lock and returns {sig, history}.
    app/api/stage2_api.py:129 · feedback
  6. ↓

    GET /api/db/feedback/<error type> (for example /api/db/feedback/T-42)
  8. ↓

    review.js loadHistory(sig) counts positive and negative rows, shows the yellow callout for the newest negative one, and draws the chips and the table.
    app/static/js/review.js:167 · browser code
  10. ↓

Saved procedure (left panel)

9

replaced by a newer version · reproduced in at least 68 % of lab runs (likely)

display

What it is: The grey line next to the heading "Saved procedure (from the knowledge base)". First its status in words (procStatus): "approved by <name>" (a second admin approved it), "awaiting approval by a second admin" (reproduced in the lab, not approved), "replaced by a newer version" (another procedure of the same cause was approved later), "retired", "proposed" … Then "reproduced in at least X % of lab runs" with a word: X is the 95 % lower bound (Wilson) of the lab runs that showed the defect, "very likely" from 80 %, "likely" from 50 %, "possible" from 25 %, else "unlikely".

Why it exists: A saved procedure is only trustworthy if a second person approved it and the lab reproduced the defect with it; the lower bound instead of the plain rate stops six lucky runs from looking like 100 %.

When: Shown when the lookup found a saved procedure for this error type.

Example from this installation: Here: "replaced by a newer version · reproduced in at least 68 % of lab runs (likely)" - procedure 074e18b2… (status superseded, repro_lower95 0.676, approved_by second_admin). The view dates from 26 Oct 2026 14:50; a new lookup would show the current approved version of the same cause instead.

admin feedback rating 0.73 from 9 decisions (1 = always judged correct)

display

What it is: The end of the same grey line: the rating of the link "cause → this procedure" = a ÷ (a + b), where a and b are the success and failure counters of that link (both start at 1, so an unjudged procedure has 0.5), and n = the number of judgements. Accept adds to a; Reject, Could not be reproduced and Restart (on a procedure) add to b; every procedure the lab validates adds one judgement too (a when at least 50 % reproduced, else b). Revising the procedure shrinks both toward 1 (×0.7); a and b together are capped at 50.

Why it exists: Learning from feedback without training: the counters are the memory of every decision, and the rating decides how high the procedure ranks next time.

When: Shown with the saved procedure.

Example from this installation: Here: rating 0.73 from 9 decisions for procedure 074e18b2… The candidate list below says "admins judged it 18 times" for the same procedure, because the lookup adds the procedure's own counters (pnode) to the link's (pedge).

26

Top candidates (what the knowledge-base lookup found for this error type, best match first)

table

What it is: A numbered list of the five records the knowledge-base lookup ranked highest for this defect, best first. A record can be a saved procedure, a possible cause, a note (lesson), an earlier judged case of the error type, or the error type itself. Each line has a title, a status, the match percentage, how often admins judged it and why it matched (entries below).

Why it exists: The project asks that a recurring defect is recognised and its stored solution offered first; showing the five best matches with their reasons lets the manager check the lookup instead of trusting a single answer.

When: Shown after the lookup.

29

lookup match 96 % (100 % = identical to the stored record)

display

What it is: The lookup's final score as a percentage: the merged score of the five comparisons (1 = first in every comparison) × √(0.5 + 0.5 × the admin rating) × e^(0.5 × tanh(ranking score)). A record often judged correct keeps its full score, one always judged wrong keeps 71 %; the ranking score from "Record my ranking" can raise it by up to 65 % - so the value can exceed 100 % and "100 % = identical" is only a rough guide.

Why it exists: One number to compare candidates; the feedback factors are deliberately mild so a well-liked record cannot lock out a better match.

When: Shown for every candidate.

Example from this installation: Here 96 %, 93 %, 93 %, 64 %, 62 %.

why it matched: text similarity 0.95, evidence-row sequence LCS 1.00, admin feedback posterior 0.75 over 18 signals

display

What it is: The reasons the lookup gives for the match, after the page drops the technical ones (word score BM25, "structured match", "lexical", "idf"). In lookups saved before 27 Oct 2026 (like this one) they are numbers: "text similarity" (letter-triplet similarity of the texts, 1 = same text), "evidence-row sequence LCS" (longest common subsequence of the packet kinds around the defect, earlier positions weigh more; 1 = same order), "admin feedback posterior 0.75 over 18 signals" (the rating a ÷ (a + b) and n), "no admin feedback yet (prior 0.50)", "exploration slot (Thompson sample)". The current code writes plain sentences instead: "same error type", "same first rule", "same firmware", "same packet sequence around the first abnormal packet", "judged correct N times, not correct M times" or "not judged yet".

Why it exists: The manager must be able to see why the system thinks a record fits, not just a score.

When: Shown when at least one reason is left after filtering.

Step 1 · Which record is the decision about?

34

Which record is the decision about?

checkbox

What it is: One checkbox row per candidate (same title, timing and status as the list above), plus "The saved procedure shown above" when the saved procedure is not among the candidates. The value of each box is the record id the server understands: "sol::<procedure hash>" for a procedure, "cause::<error type>::<cause id>" for a cause, "case::…", "sig::…", "lesson::…" for the others. The help line says: tick one; Prefer, Tie and Mark as a duplicate take two (Link to another takes one: the procedure to copy); decisions about the defect as a whole need none. The ticked ids are sent in screen order as "targets"; for two-record decisions the first ticked (higher in the list) comes first.

Why it exists: Every verdict must name exactly which record it is about, so the credit or blame lands on that record only ("localized blame": records the admin did not touch are not punished).

When: Shown after the lookup; "No record to tick: nothing is saved for this error type yet." when the lookup found nothing.

Step 2 · Judge the ticked procedure

37

Accept

button

What it is: Tile text: "Accept" — Correct (+1): this procedure is right; it is re-run in the lab, then the test script is written. Tags: "needs one ticked record", "runs in the lab, takes minutes". Colour: green. Gives one success (+1) to the ticked record and starts the lab work. On a procedure: +1 on the procedure and on its link from the cause, and +1 on the cause; the saved procedure is then run first as a safety check ("regression guard"): if it still shows the defect in at least 3 of 6 runs it is reused (no search), otherwise a lesson is written and the search starts from it. On a cause: +1 on the cause and a new search for a procedure. Ticking an "earlier case" gives no credit (that kind of record has no counters) and starts a search from scratch. Same as "Correct" on a card of the main screen.

Why it exists: The project's positive feedback: an admin confirmation must strengthen exactly the confirmed record, and a confirmed procedure must be re-validated on the device before it becomes a regression test.

When: Offered whenever the lookup found at least one record.

Example from this installation: Scratch copy, Accept on the saved procedure: events admin_action, proc_credit, verdict, then solution_propose + solution_validate (stress variant) and two script_gate; cause edge a 2.0 → 2.98 (fade, then +1), n 1 → 2, ta 1 → 2; procedure link a 2 → 3; procedure node a 1 → 2. Live: the newest Accept on T-42 (27 Oct 2026 12:57:54, admin) shows "✓ regression test filed found on known-bad firmware 6/6 · on fixed firmware 0/3".
How it works, step by step
  1. You
    You tick one record, click "Accept", then "Record: Accept" (the key a opens the same step).
  2. ↓
  3. Browser
    startAction("accept") marks the tile and opens step 3; no extra field is shown; confirmAction re-checks missing() and calls doAction, which sends the ticked records, your name, the note and, when filled, the change text, the order and the decision number (a second admin's name only for Approve as second admin, Retire the procedure and Approve the deletion).
    app/static/js/review.js:267 · browser code
  4. ↓
  5. Request
    POST /api/runs/<run>/incidents/<defect>/act {"action": "accept", "targets": ["sol::<hash>"], "requester": "<your name>", "approver": "", "note": ""} (approver always empty here)
  6. ↓
  7. Server address
    stage2_api.act checks that stage 1 has finished and that stage 2 was started for this run (otherwise 409), then passes the decision to the stage-2 service. A refusal from the decision itself comes back as "action_error" inside a normal 200 answer.
    app/api/stage2_api.py:290 · act
  8. ↓
  9. Service
    Stage2Service.act sees a lab decision (one of SEARCH_ACTIONS in stage2/stage2_v3.py) and queues it as a background job (job table in db/app.sqlite); the answer {"job": id} comes back at once. The job (Stage2Service._execute_job) takes the stage-2 lock, runs Stage2V3.execute, commits and records the result.
    app/stage2_service.py:228 · Stage2Service._execute_job
  10. ↓
  11. Engine
    Stage2V3.execute first calls admin_actions.apply with your decision and the list of records the lookup showed; apply always writes one admin_action event first (decision, targets, ranking, note, second admin, shown records, run, defect), then the branch for this decision. Branch accept: for a procedure it logs proc_credit {edge_id: "REPRODUCED_BY|<type>::<cause>|scn::<hash>", node_id: "scn::<hash>", r: 1.0} and verdict {verdict: "correct", chosen: <cause>, lab_result: true}; for a cause only the verdict. Effect text: "marked correct (+1)".
    stage2/admin_actions.py:136 · apply
  12. ↓
  13. Database
    verdict → KGDB._project: first every cause of this error type fades 2 % toward the start (a = 1 + (a − 1) × 0.98, the same for b), then the chosen cause gets a + 1, n + 1 (a + b capped at 50) and, because lab_result is true, ta + 1; the defect's tokens go into case_memory. proc_credit → ProcGraph: the cause → procedure link (pedge) and the procedure (pnode) each a + 1, n + 1.
    stage2/kgdb.py:213 · KGDB._project
  14. ↓
  15. Engine
    Lab: a procedure of the same error type → mode reuse: it is run 6 times on the device model; 3 or more reproductions → status reused_validated, stress step, then _finish; fewer → lesson "the saved procedure no longer shows the error on …" and mode adapt (search). A cause → mode generate: AI (artificial intelligence) proposal, search under 300 trials and the 600 s triage limit, shortening, stress step. _finish checks the procedure on known-bad firmware (6 runs) and fixed firmware (3 runs): passed = found at least once on known-bad and never on fixed → test files and a script_gate event; new procedures get solution_propose + solution_validate. _finish would also approve a new procedure when the request names a second admin, but the page sends that name only with Approve / Retire / Approve the deletion, so a lab decision made here approves nothing.
    stage2/stage2_v3.py:217 · Stage2V3.execute
  16. ↓
  17. Files
    suite/<test id>/manifest.json, test_<test id>.py and conftest.py for every procedure that passed the lab check (emit_closed_loop_test); the result is appended to runs/<run>/stage2/<defect>.json and db/stage2_log.jsonl.
  18. ↓
  19. Screen
    Receipt: "What happens next: the accepted procedure is re-run first as a safety check. button

What it is: Tile text: "Revise the text" — change the stored text of the ticked cause or the notes on a procedure (text in step 3); nothing runs in the lab and the earlier counts are reduced; to change the steps and run them use Needs changes on a card or the editor. Stores your corrected text (the JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) in "Text of your change") as a new version of the ticked record and shrinks its old evidence toward neutral (both counters × 0.7), because the counts were earned by the old content. On a cause the text becomes a new node version; on a procedure it is stored as "admin_revision" (notes) on the link cause → procedure - the procedure's steps are not changed. No credit is given and, as the tile says, nothing runs in the lab (revise is not one of the lab decisions); to change the steps and have them run, use the editor below ("Propose my procedure and run it on the device") or "Needs changes" on a card. The effect text the server returns, shown in the Result tab's Action row, says the same: "revised: the stored text was changed; nothing was run in the lab; the earlier counts were reduced".

Why it exists: A record can be partly right; changing its content without throwing away its history, but with less weight, is the honest way to record "partially correct".

Record my ranking

button

What it is: Tile text: "Record my ranking" — your order, best first (this does not count as "correct"). Tags: "needs an order (click the candidates)". Records the order you built by clicking candidates as a rating only (Plackett–Luce): the first record's ranking score rises by 0.3 × (1 − its predicted chance of being first) ÷ number of items, the others fall by their share. Causes and procedures are ranked separately and only when at least two of the same kind are in your order; "earlier case" lines are ignored. a, b and n never change. NOTE: if your order holds fewer than two procedures (or causes), nothing is recorded, yet the receipt still says the order was recorded.

Why it exists: An order ("this one before that one") is a different signal from "correct"; mixing them would let a mere preference count as proof.

When: Offered whenever the lookup found at least one record.

Example from this installation: Scratch copy, two procedures: proc_rank, pl 0 → +0.075 for the first and −0.075 for the second (0.3 × 0.5 ÷ 2).

Approve as second admin

button

What it is: Tile text: "Approve as second admin" — approve this procedure so it is used as the saved procedure. Tags: "needs one ticked record", "needs a second admin". Colour: yellow (two people). The four-eyes approval of a procedure the lab has reproduced: its status becomes "approved by <second admin>" and any earlier approved procedure of the same cause becomes "replaced by a newer version". It only takes effect if the procedure is "awaiting approval" (validated in the lab) and the second admin is not the one who produced it; otherwise the event is recorded but nothing changes - the message still shows the receipt "The procedure is now approved …" and the Result tab says "approved" or "status is now …". A real approval also adds +1 to the procedure node.

Why it exists: Two-person rule: nothing becomes the reference regression test on one person's word, and nothing is approved that the lab has not reproduced.

When: Offered only when the lookup found a record and says seen before = match or ambiguous.

Example from this installation: Scratch copy: same name as approver → refused, no event; with "mapper two" → solution_approve (actor mapper two), status validated-by-execution → admin-approved, node a 2 → 3. Sent again on the approved procedure → a second solution_approve that changes nothing, message still "approved".
How it works, step by step

Split

button

What it is: Tile text: "Split" — split a cause in two. Tags: "needs one ticked record". Creates a new cause next to the ticked one and gives the ticked one a new version. Add a cause

button

What it is: Tile text: "Add a cause" — my own description of the cause. Tags: "runs in the lab, takes minutes". Colour: green. Saves your own explanation of the cause as a new cause of this error type (id "c<number of active causes>") with one success (+1); if you ticked an existing cause, that one gets one failure (−1). Then a lab job searches for a procedure that reproduces your cause and checks it on known-bad and fixed firmware. The text goes into "Text of your change" as JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) {"text": "…"}; when empty, the note is used.

Why it exists: When the stored causes are all wrong, the admin's own diagnosis must become a first-class record that the lab then tries to prove.

Generate test cases

button

What it is: Tile text: "Generate test cases" — make more test variants from the saved command sequences; each is run on the drive and kept only if the same error appears. Tags: "runs in the lab, takes minutes". The AI (artificial intelligence) reviewer composes up to three test variants from the procedures saved for this error type (and up to two of the same failure family), for example a robust recreation, the trigger at its timing boundary, a different path to the same state; code checks them, each runs 6 times and is kept when the lower bound reaches 50 %; if none is, the search changes the best one (up to 120 trials). Every kept variant is checked on known-bad and fixed firmware and filed with its sources. Nothing is approved automatically. Ticked records are not used. Same as "Generate test cases" on the main screen.

Why it exists: The project asks for more than one test per defect; composing from proven procedures is cheaper than searching from scratch.

When: Offered always. Not shown on this page, because its saved lookup predates this decision.

Try nearby variations

button

What it is: Tile text: "Try nearby variations" — try the procedure with each timing halved and doubled, every power state and a longer burst; variants that still show the error are saved as tests. Tags: "runs in the lab, takes minutes". Takes the newest approved procedure of this error type (else the newest awaiting approval; ticked records are not used) and tries its neighbourhood: each timing value halved and doubled, every other power state, the last command repeated, and injected link faults when the bench supports them. Each variant runs 3 times; 2 or more reproductions = failure-prone. The three most stressful failure-prone variants are checked on known-bad and fixed firmware and filed as tests. Nothing is approved automatically. Same as "Try nearby variations" on the main screen.

Why it exists: The project asks for vulnerability analysis: knowing which nearby conditions also fail tells the firmware team how wide the weakness is, and the tests guard the margin.

When: Offered always. Not shown on this page, because its saved lookup predates this decision.

59

Restart the search after a failed attempt

button

What it is: Tile text: "Restart the search after a failed attempt" — failed trial (-1): recorded against the ticked procedure or cause; the search starts again with another random seed. Tags: "needs one ticked record", "runs in the lab, takes minutes". The "Negative Ack (−1)" of the project's flow: records the failed attempt and starts the search again on another random stream. With a cause ticked: b + 1 and the lab counter tb + 1 on it; with a procedure ticked: b + 1 on its link from the cause (and the lab then re-runs that procedure first, as with Accept); always a lesson "FAILED TRIAL recorded by <you>; the search starts again: <note>". The attempt number = how many earlier results of this defect ended without a reproduction; the search seed is shifted by 10 per attempt. The tile needs one ticked record ("Before recording: tick the record this is about (step 1)"), so the −1 is recorded against it - except when the ticked record is an "earlier case" or the error type itself, which have no counters: then only the lesson is written and the effect text is empty. NOTE: the history still counts this decision as neutral, not negative.

Why it exists: A search that found nothing must count against what was tried, and simply repeating the same random search would repeat the same failure.

When: Offered always. Not shown on this page, because its saved lookup predates this decision. The Result box of the main screen offers the same after a failed search.

Example from this installation: Scratch copy, cause ticked: two verdicts (c0 b 1.96 → 2.90, tb 2 → 3) and the lesson, then a new search. (Sent with nothing ticked - no longer possible from the tile - only the lesson was written.)

62

Undo a decision

button

What it is: Tile text: "Undo a decision" — undo one event by its number (shown as # in the decision history and on the Knowledge base page); the tables are rebuilt without it. Tags: "asks which decision". Marks ONE event of the knowledge base as undone and rebuilds every table from the remaining events, so its effect disappears. You give the event number: the history table below shows it as "#<number>" next to the date, and the Knowledge base page lists every event. NOTE: one decision consists of several events (admin_action + verdict / proc_credit / lesson / …), and the # in the history is the number of its admin_action event. Undoing that number only removes the row from the history and leaves the counters as they are; undoing a primitive event (number from the Knowledge base page) reverses the counters but leaves the history row. Only the Undo button in the message right after a decision undoes all of that decision's events at once.

Why it exists: Every change is an event, so every change can be reversed exactly; mistakes must be correctable without editing the database by hand.

When: Offered whenever the lookup found at least one record.

Example from this installation: Scratch copy: undoing event 55 (the solution_deprecate of a Retire) brought the procedure back to admin-approved and its node b 3 → 2, while the Retire row (its admin_action, event 54) stayed in the history as negative. Queue depth

field

What it is: Timing value "Queue depth" = how many commands are outstanding at the same time. Allowed 1–256 (default 8 when the loaded procedure has none). A value outside the range makes the preview show "queue depth must be 1-256" in red and disables the propose button. Sent as timing.qd.

Why it exists: Timing is often what makes a defect appear (a command too soon after a power transition); the ranges are what the bench can set, and the server clamps to the same ranges (compose.TIMING_RANGES).

Propose my procedure and run it on the device

button

What it is: Sends your version as the decision "Add a procedure" (add_procedure) with the procedure as content: it is saved as "proposed" under your name and run in the lab first; if it shows the defect in at least 3 of 6 runs it is validated, checked on known-bad and fixed firmware and filed as a regression test; otherwise it is marked "failed validation", a lesson says so and the search starts from it. The ticked records of step 1 are sent too (a ticked cause becomes the procedure's cause).

Why it exists: The admin's knowledge is used, but the lab - not the admin - decides whether it reproduces the defect (the project's "validated by execution" rule).

When: Inside the open editor; disabled while the preview lists a problem.

Example from this installation: Scratch copy (aspm_idle → read, D3hot): solution_propose by admin:mapper one, 0 of 6 reproductions → failed-validation and the lesson, then a search that found and filed a reproducing procedure.
How it works, step by step
  1. You
    You click "Propose my procedure and run it on the device".
  2. ↓
  3. Browser
    The handler shows "proposing your procedure and validating it in the lab…" and calls doAction("add_procedure", edScenario()).
    app/static/js/review.js:84 · browser code
  4. ↓
  5. Request
    POST /api/runs/<run>/incidents/<defect>/act {"action": "add_procedure", "content": {"commands": [{"op": "flush"}, {"op": "write"}], "timing": {"qd": 8, "inter_cmd_us": 200, "bs_kb": 4, "burst_len": 16, "idle_gap_ms": 1866}, "power_state": "none"}, "targets": [...], …}
  6. ↓
  7. Server address
    stage2_api.act checks that stage 1 has finished and that stage 2 was started for this run (otherwise 409), then passes the decision to the stage-2 service. A refusal from the decision itself comes back as "action_error" inside a normal 200 answer.
    app/api/stage2_api.py:290 · act
  8. ↓
  9. Service
    Stage2Service.act sees a lab decision (one of SEARCH_ACTIONS in stage2/stage2_v3.py) and queues it as a background job (job table in db/app.sqlite); the answer {"job": id} comes back at once. The job (Stage2Service._execute_job) takes the stage-2 lock, runs Stage2V3.execute, commits and records the result.
    app/stage2_service.py:228 · Stage2Service._execute_job
  10. ↓
  11. Engine
    admin_actions.apply → clean_scenario, then solution_propose {producer: "admin:<you>"} (status proposed).
    stage2/admin_actions.py:274 · apply
  12. ↓
  13. Engine
    Stage2V3.execute: 6 runs; ≥ 3 → stress step and _finish (solution_validate under its hash, lab check, script_gate, test files); else solution_validate 0.0, lesson "your procedure showed the error in k of 6 runs - not enough; the search starts from it", search.
    stage2/stage2_v3.py:217 · Stage2V3.execute
  14. ↓
  15. Files
    suite/<test id>/manifest.json, test_<test id>.py and conftest.py for every procedure that passed the lab check (emit_closed_loop_test); the result is appended to runs/<run>/stage2/<defect>.json and db/stage2_log.jsonl.
  16. ↓
  17. Screen
    Receipt "What happens next: your procedure is run first in the lab; if it reproduces the defect it is kept as validated in the lab (under your name) and checked on known-bad and fixed firmware. Approving it as the saved procedure is a separate decision by a second admin.", progress, then "stage 2 finished: …" with Undo and the outcome in the Result tab.

Earlier decisions on this error type

93

Earlier decisions on this error type

table

What it is: The table of earlier decisions on this error type from every run and defect, newest first, at most 50 rows, with the columns When (with the event number "#<n>" used by Undo), Who, Decision, Reason or note, Lab outcome. Undone decisions are left out. A decision the server refused after logging it (for example Mark as a duplicate on procedures, Split on a procedure, Approve the deletion by the requester) is still listed, because its admin_action event was written first.

Why it exists: History of feedback per error type is a project requirement; it lets the next admin see what was tried and how it ended.

When: Shown after the lookup; "no decision recorded for this error type yet" when empty.

Example from this installation: Here 50 rows; the newest: 27 Oct 2026 12:59:54 #1169, admin, Try nearby variations, no note, "✓ regression test filed found on known-bad firmware 6/6 · on fixed firmware 0/3".

When (# = event number, for Undo)

row

What it is: The local date and time of the admin_action event (the event's ts, seconds since 1970, shown with the browser's date format), followed by its event number in grey, for example "#1169". That number is what "Which decision to undo" asks for; it undoes this admin_action event only (the row disappears, the counters stay) - the Undo button right after a decision undoes all of its events.

Why it exists: Order and age of the decisions matter (old feedback fades 2 % per verdict, the newest negative one is shown in the callout), and the number makes each row addressable for Undo.

When: One cell per history row.

The message after a decision

119

Undo

button

What it is: After a decision a dark message appears at the top right with the receipt or the effects (8 s; 3 s for the quiet saves of the main screen) and an "Undo" button. Undo marks every event the decision itself wrote (action_events: the admin_action and the verdict / credit / lesson events) as undone, newest first, rebuilds the knowledge base and refreshes the page; the message then says "undone". For a lab decision the Undo comes with the second message "stage 2 finished: <outcome>"; it removes the decision's credit, but the procedures, lab checks and test files the lab produced remain. A refused decision shows "refused: …" without Undo.

Why it exists: Every mistake must be reversible in one click, right after it happened.

When: Shown after each decision; hides itself after a few seconds.

Example from this installation: Scratch copy: the Accept on the saved procedure returned action_events [14, 15, 16] (admin_action, proc_credit, verdict); Undo would post 16, 15, 14.
How it works, step by step
  1. You
    You click "Undo" in the message.
  2. ↓
  3. Browser
    undoFor(result) loops over result.action_events in reverse and posts each one.
    app/static/js/review.js:307 · browser code
  4. ↓
  5. Request
    POST /api/db/undo {"event_id": <n>, "actor": "<your name>"} (once per event)
  6. ↓
  7. Server address
    db_api.undo requires event_id and calls the service.
    app/api/db_api.py:67 · undo
  8. ↓
  9. Service
    Stage2Service.undo: under the lock KGDB.undo, then the lookup index is rebuilt.
    app/stage2_service.py:326 · Stage2Service.undo
  10. ↓

Buttons and links

1

Build or refresh the report

button

What it is: The blue button at the top of the Report card. It asks the server for this run's report and for the key results of every run, then redraws everything in the card below it. Opening Step 5 with a run selected does the same automatically.

Why it exists: The project statement asks for the time taken by each stage to be reported explicitly, and for key results such as first-level triage time, automatic isolation and tests generated. The report is computed afresh from the saved timings and decisions every time, so it can never be stale after another decision in step 4.

When: Step 5 unlocks once a run is selected and its stage 1 has finished (main.js unlocked). With no run selected the button only shows "select a run first". The button does not reload the Generated regression tests card; that list is read when the page is opened.
