runs within the first-level triage limit (10 min)

display

What it is: Shown as "<runs within> / <runs>". A run is within the limit when the seconds of its timed stage-1 steps add up to no more than 600. The 600 seconds (and the "10 min" in the label) come from the fixed constant FIRST_LEVEL_TRIAGE_S in stage2/loop_rules.py, not from the Settings field "First-level triage limit in seconds", which limits the stage-2 search per defect instead.

Why it exists: The system diagram's rule: more than 10 minutes of first-level triage is a fail.

display

What it is: One line under the chips: the two rules of the system diagram (score above 0.9 in 3 lab runs in a row = optimal; first-level triage over 10 min = fail), the minutes of automatic triage measured over all runs, and three recurrence counts: defects seen again in a later capture, re-run in the lab, caught again by their test. The rule numbers are the constants of stage2/loop_rules.py: changing "Optimal = … in a row" in Settings does not change this line. The "score" is in fact checks passed out of 3 (same error type, same rule, confirmed).

Why it exists: Shows the yardstick next to the results, so the chips can be read without the documentation.

2

How the AI reviewer is reached (backend)

select

What it is: Config key llm.backend. cli = the claude command-line login on this machine (no key); sdk = the Anthropic API or a company gateway (base URL + key variable); openai-compat = any chat-completions endpoint; auto = sdk when a key is set, else cli; standin = no model, fixed answers (tests). In stage 2 the new choice is used at once after Save; if it cannot be reached (no claude command, no key) the stand-in is used silently and the message line says "stand-in". Stage 1 uses it from the next run started: openai-compat and standin make stage 1's second opinion run without a model (dry-run). The value is part of the run key, so an identical CSV is analysed afresh instead of reused.

Why it exists: Production reaches the model through a company gateway; laptops use the command-line login.

When: With server.lock_endpoint true (deploy/config.production.example.json) a change is refused with 403 and nothing is saved.

Example from this installation: cli in this installation; sdk in deploy/config.production.example.json.

Stage 2

6

First-level triage limit in seconds (600 = 10 minutes)

field

What it is: Config key stage2.time_budget_s. Applied at once after Save. When a stage-2 search starts, deadline = start + this many seconds; past it the search stops and the result is marked "first-level triage limit (10 min) exceeded". 0, or an empty field (sent as 0), switches the limit off; the value is not checked. The Report's "runs within the first-level triage limit" chip does not use this field.

Why it exists: The system diagram's rule: more than 10 minutes of first-level triage is a fail.

field

Save

18

Save

button

What it is: Sends every field of this page in one request, plus two fields of Step 1: the firmware label and namespace size typed there become the defaults stage1.firmware_label and stage1.nsze. The server merges the values, writes the whole configuration to config/app_config.json and rebuilds the AI reviewer and the stage-2 limits at once (Stage2Service.reload_llm). Bench, the allowed trace folders and the server address and port need a restart; the model, backend, batch and capture-check settings reach stage 1 with the next run started. The AI reviewer usage counters restart from zero (a new AI reviewer object). A server started with --standin writes backend standin into the file on the next Save.

Why it exists: The statement: "in the production environment put the final API URL and model name". The lock (server.lock_endpoint) stops anyone who reaches the page from redirecting the key, turning on web search or widening the readable folders.

When: With server.lock_endpoint true, a change of llm.base_url, llm.api_key_env, llm.backend, llm.tools or paths.allowed_csv_roots is refused with 403 and nothing at all is saved.

Example from this installation: On a scratch copy started with --standin, Save answered {"llm_active": "stand-in", "ok": true} and the file then held backend "standin" and the Step-1 firmware label; with server.lock_endpoint true, a new base URL answered 403 "llm.base_url is locked by server.lock_endpoint: stop the service, edit the config file, start it again".
How it works, step by step
  1. You
    You press Save.
  2. ↓
  3. Browser
    Collects the fields into {llm, stage2, stage1}.
    app/static/js/settings.js:11 · browser code
  4. ↓
  5. Request
    PUT /api/config {llm: {backend, model, effort, base_url, api_key_env, batch, capture_check}, stage2: {bench, opt_budget, time_budget_s, optimal_consecutive, stress_trials, n_bad, n_fixed, search_on}, stage1: {firmware_label, nsze}}
  6. ↓
  7. Server address
    put_config(): lock check, merge of the sections llm, stage1, stage2, paths, write, reload.
    app/api/config_api.py:24 · put_config
  8. ↓
  9. Server address
    save_config(): writes every key except the internal _path; the help notes inside the sections are kept.
    app/api/config_api.py:11 · save_config
  10. ↓
  11. Service
    reload_llm(): new AI reviewer; opt_budget, optimizer, time_budget_s, stress_trials, optimal_consecutive, n_bad, n_fixed, search_on copied into the running engine.
    app/stage2_service.py:86 · Stage2Service.reload_llm
  12. ↓

    config/app_config.json rewritten.
  14. ↓

    The message line under the Save button says "saved · the AI reviewer now in use: …" (or "could not save: …").
The code behind it (3 excerpts)
19

saved · the AI reviewer now in use: …

display

What it is: The line next to Save: "saved · the AI reviewer now in use: <name>", plus "· the Bench change takes effect after a restart of the application" when Bench changed, or "could not save: <reason>". The name is the plain form made by llmWord() in main.js from the server's internal name: anthropic:claude-haiku-5-5:low becomes "Anthropic claude-haiku-5-5" (the effort is left out), stand-in becomes "stand-in (no model)". The sidebar's "AI reviewer" badge gets the same plain name, so it reads as it did at page load. The "lab device" badge is not touched by Save.

Why it exists: Confirms which AI reviewer is really in use after the change; a backend that cannot be reached shows up here as stand-in.

When: Empty until Save is pressed.

Example from this installation: On the scratch copy: "saved · the AI reviewer now in use: Anthropic claude-haiku-5-5", badge "Anthropic claude-haiku-5-5" before and after; with Bench changed to hook the line ended "· the Bench change takes effect after a restart of the application" and the lab device badge stayed "simulated device".

2

Word / Meaning

table

What it is: 37 rows, in the order the words are met: Defect, Error type, the catalogue, Error family, AI reviewer, Confirmed / Suspect / Needs evidence, Procedure, Lab run, Reproduced in at least X %, Score, First-level triage limit, Regression test, Knowledge base, Key results and others. Three rows do not match the code: "Key results" describes a list (defects found, reproduced, tests, still open) that is not what the report's chips show; "verdict reused from the cache" says the same error family was confirmed earlier, while the cache key is error type, rule, family, layer, rule set, evidence-row sequence, model and prompt version, and non-confirmed verdicts are reused too; "First-level triage limit" is stage 2's time per defect, while the report's chip of that name applies the fixed 600 s to stage 1 per run.

Why it exists: One reference for all terms. The same words are produced by the translation helpers in api.js and decision.js; the two are kept in step by hand.

admin feedback rating … from … decisions (1 = always judged correct)

display

What it is: a ÷ (a + b) of the link from the error type to this cause, with n decisions. a grows with every "correct" verdict and b with every "not correct" (both start at 1; each new verdict first shrinks the older counts a little, and editing the cause's text shrinks them more).

Why it exists: The learned belief that this cause is the right one, from the admins' feedback; it orders the causes.

Event log (most recent first)

table

What it is: The most recent events: 25 at page load, 60 after a click on the tab or refresh, and redrawn by itself after a successful Undo (the new undo event on top). Six columns: event number, time, what happened, who, details, undone. The knowledge base is event-sourced: this append-only list of everything that happened is the only thing ever written by a decision or a lab result; every other table is computed from it.

64

Undo this event & rebuild

button

What it is: After a confirmation ("Undo event N and rebuild the knowledge base from the event log?") the event is undone. Nothing is deleted: the event is marked undone = 1, a new event of kind undo is added, every computed table is emptied (node, node_version, edge, case_memory, signature, artifact, solution, lesson and the procedure graph pnode, pnode_version, pedge) and every other event is replayed in order. The result is exactly as if the undone event had never happened, including what later events built on it. The search index is then rebuilt. Files outside the knowledge base stay: test folders in suite/, the run's stage-2 state files and the verdict cache. The person is always recorded as admin; a number that does not exist still adds an undo event; undoing an undo event changes nothing (there is no redo). After a successful undo the page shows the message "event N undone; the knowledge base was rebuilt from the event log" for about 6 seconds, and redraws the counts at the top (overview()) and the event list (loadEvents()) at once, with no reload: the new undo event is at the top of the list and the undone event carries the "undone" pill. When the server refuses, the message says "undo failed: <reason>".

Why it exists: Every change must be reversible, without editing the history: an audit can always see what was done and undone.

When: Asks for confirmation first; nothing happens with an empty number.

Example from this installation: On a scratch copy (never on the live database): undoing event 3, a lesson, answered {"undone": 3}; lessons went from 1 to 0 and event 4 (undo, details {"event_id": 3}) was added. Pressed in the page (current db.html and db.js) for event 8, a lesson: the message "event 8 undone; the knowledge base was rebuilt from the event log" appeared and hid itself after about 6 s; without a reload the chips went from 8 to 9 events logged and from 1 to 0 lessons, the list's top row became event 9 (undo, {"event_id":8}) and event 8 showed the "undone" pill; no script errors.

Where the screen and the code still differ (known limitations)

While mapping every element, four reviewers compared each screen text with the code. Mismatches that could be fixed safely were fixed in the code on 27 October 2026 (for example: the second-admin name is no longer reused by a later decision; "also retire it" asks for the second admin; "Look up again" really looks up again; Undo on the Knowledge base page shows its message; the tile texts of Revise, Link, Add a procedure, Undo, Restart and Prefer now say what the code does). These remain, described in their entries:

WhereWhat differs
Defect pageWhen the AI reviewer picks a lower-ranked error type, the page shows that id with the top candidate's title; steps 2–4 keep the top candidate.
Steps 2/3 vs defect pageA defect can read "Suspect" in the list and "Confirmed" on its page (the page uses the final isolation record).
Step 1Host tool records alone (without dmesg) can make stage 1 fail with "cannot align clocks".
Defect page, section 5"What usually fixes it" shows the catalogue's "test to provoke it" text for most error types.
Step 1The reuse check ignores name, device, firmware and run label: analysing the same file again opens the old run.
Step 4, historyRemoving, ranking or approving marks the defect "decided"; Defer also counts as decided.
Step 4, UndoUndo removes the decision's events, not the procedures and tests a lab job already produced.
Step 4, LinkA linked procedure stays "proposed"; the lookup does not offer proposed procedures, so it cannot be accepted from the screens yet.
Step 4, SplitThe suggested JSON for Split leaves the old cause's text empty unless you fill it in.
Step 4, older lookupsA lookup stored before 27 October shows 23 tiles and older seen-before words; "Look up again" refreshes it.
Report and Knowledge base"Regression tests" counts every lab check, filed or not; the rules line uses the fixed constants (600 s, 3 in a row), not the Settings values; "links between causes and procedures" counts all graph links.
Knowledge baseThe AI reviewer chip shows the internal model name; the filter does not search family names.
SettingsSave also stores step 1's firmware label and namespace size; a server started with --standin writes "standin" into the config file.

End of the application map.
